macos_sixteen_fe_attribution.finding: sixteen-fe-t1 is the one Mac regression (candidate 0.413 s vs beta.8 0.389 s and beta.9 0.390 s in all six blocks, +6%; same 14/9 LSMR iterations, diagonal preconditioner, projection phase 0.271 vs 0.247 s). Linux runs the same cell 6% faster than beta.9.
macos_sixteen_fe_attribution.measurement: development attribution, not qualification: arm64 release builds of the integration head with within StepKernel::Fused (the shipped default) and StepKernel::Separate, alternated with the qualification candidate and beta.9 plugins on the routing cells (medians of 6-8 native calls each, Mac M2 Ultra)
macos_sixteen_fe_attribution.bits: the Separate variant reproduces beta.9 output columns bit for bit on every cell; the Fused variant reproduces the candidate, so the entire many-FE science difference against beta.9 is the fused step kernel (declared scope)
macos_sixteen_fe_attribution.conclusion: the within fused LSMR step (080d65e..3b5b9b9a) is the cause: +6% at sixteen effects and one worker on arm64, neutral at four workers, and the source of the 8-16% one-worker gains on three, four and eight effects. No fereg-side kernel fence was added. Johannes accepted the one-cell Mac exception on 2026-10-28; a within follow-up for many small unsorted intercept terms on arm64 remains open.
